newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle trade to swing on weather-feedlot.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle trade to swing on weather-feedlot.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets next week were seen largely controlled by the weather, feedlot sources said.
If forecasts for continued extreme cold and possible snow storms next week prove accurate, the weather could underpin fed cattle prices, feedlot sources said.

Cattle this week sold at $65.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from last week. Early weakness was somewhat tempered by outlooks for extremely cold weather to sweep inot the Plains late this week, which generated brisk packer buying, the sources said.
Most weekly showlists were sold and feedlots were current.
Several feedyards sold cattle from next week's list to meet the strong demand, they said.

Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots sold 106,900 head this week, USDA reported. The showlist had been estimated by market sources at 70,000 head. Kansas feedlots sold 107,100 head, above the estimated showlist of 87,400.

Temperatures in the key areas of Nebraska, Kansas and the Texas/Oklahoma Panhandle were seen staying below to much below normal next week, which could cut weight gains at a time when cattle weights are already well under those of a year ago.
USDA estimated slaughter cattle weights this week at 1,162 lbs, just under 1,163 last week but well below 1,198 a year ago.
Forecasts for a major snowstorm late Monday and Tuesday for Nebraska and Tuesday, followed by windy, cold weather, could stress cattle further, they said.
